title: Refine implicit-surface weights with chain-aware influence domains
description:
## Explicit anatomy requirement

The weighting system must remain general-purpose: it must not assume biped or quadruped topology. Any number of limbs, in any authored order and at any valid Body position, must be supported without limb-count modes or species-specific branches.

## Summary
Refine the MVP welded-surface weighting model with explicit anatomical influence domains and prove that posed body/limb motion does not create visibly incorrect cross-body smearing.

## User Mandate
> "the elbow is moving the upper arm" but only in terms of the animation weights, I think. The actual transform heirarchy is fine, it's more that I would expect the rotating the foream/elbow to only affect the downstream sections of the arm

STRICT. Rotating the forearm/elbow bone must only affect the downstream sections of that limb in the animation weights; the upper arm must not visibly follow. This is a locality requirement on the authored BoneWeights, not a Transform-hierarchy change (the hierarchy is already correct).

## Current state
The domain-aware refinement is implemented. `InfluenceDomain[]` is supplied by the live runtime preview to `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind`; Body radius preparation uses the compact anatomical Body rig; and the topology dependency is resolved. `ImplicitSurfaceInfluenceDomainResolver` now resolves a primary geometry domain plus its intended non-Body authored ancestors. Child geometry therefore may blend with its owning limb chain while sibling and opposite-side chains remain ineligible.

## Newly observed risk
User visual validation on `dinus_uprightus` shows general mesh smearing/weird deformation when Body rig parts are moved. Do not assume this is caused by chain-domain attribution alone. Characterize actual generated `BoneWeight` distributions and a controlled one-bone pose before changing the falloff radius or introducing another heuristic. The current closest-point-on-segment weighting model must be preserved unless measured evidence identifies it as the source.

## Acceptance
Preserve TSK-0131 closest-segment distance, morphology radii, deterministic top-four selection, normalization, mirror behavior, and build-time ownership. Prove hip, shoulder, mirrored, branch, knee, elbow, child-geometry, and controlled Body-segment deformation locality. A one-bone pose must not produce long-range smearing into unrelated Body regions beyond the documented blend neighborhood. The domain contract must remain independent of limb count, authored order, and attachment position.

## Remaining gate
Executable Unity generated-geometry validation is still required. The task must not be marked Done based solely on source/build inspection. Foot-grounding remains separate.

## Evidence
Focused resolver regression coverage proves child-domain inclusion, sibling exclusion, and mirrored parent-chain isolation. Generated-creature visual validation is now also required for deformation locality. See the skeleton/animation audit documents under `docs/audits/` on `audit/skeleton-animation-improvements-2026-09-07`.

## Performance note
Domain hierarchy construction is now cached once per resolved part/side during binding preparation instead of allocating a `List<string>`/array for every welded vertex. This is a build-time optimization only; it does not alter influence eligibility or the per-frame animation path.

## Mechanism note (2026-09-12)
`ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.Author` weights a vertex by closest-point-on-segment falloff: `effectiveRadius = segment.Radius * RadiusScale (3)`, `weight = pow(1 - d/effectiveRadius, 2)`, top-4, normalized. The `InfluenceDomain` gate admits the whole owning chain (`DomainId = part.Id`), so every segment of a limb competes with every other by raw 3D distance. An upper-arm vertex near the elbow is therefore inside the forearm segment's tube and blends toward the forearm bone. Whether that is a correct joint blend or excessive upstream leakage must be measured before the policy changes.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Static reproduction diagnosis: ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.Author previously threw when an explicit InfluenceDomain excluded every positive falloff candidate. The runtime binding path always supplies generated InfluenceDomain[] and therefore could abort regeneration on valid welded vertices that fell just outside the finite weighting tube. Fixed in commit 841e85ce479d0315d6f68a000d5d4d994d785a69: when a domain-constrained vertex has no positive falloff candidate, choose the nearest segment admitted by that already-resolved domain, deterministically tie-breaking by BoneIndex, with weight 1.0. No sibling/opposite-side fallback is permitted. The unrestricted helper remains strict. Unity/generated-creature deformation validation remains required.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
## Measured evidence — elbow over-reaches into the upper arm (2026-09-12)

User clarification: rotating the forearm/elbow moves the upper arm **in the animation weights** (the Transform hierarchy is correct). They expect a bone to affect only the downstream part of the chain.

Measurement taken live on the `CreatureCreator Preview` rig (`execute_code`, read-only) with arm chain `part_67fc33c4_j0` = upper arm (index 12), `part_67fc33c4_j1` = forearm (index 14); mirrored indices 13/15 gave identical numbers.

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| upper-arm segment length | 0.878 |
| upper-arm-dominant vertices | 323 |
| mean forearm weight on those vertices | 0.079 |
| max forearm weight on an upper-arm vertex | 0.383 |
| upper-arm vertices with forearm weight > 0.25 | 61 (≈19%) |
| furthest vertex with any forearm weight, distance from elbow | 0.373 (≈42% of the upper-arm segment) |

Interpretation: influence is **not** limited to the bone's own chain span. This is `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.Author` using pure closest-point-on-segment falloff with `effectiveRadius = radius * RadiusScale (3)`, squared falloff, and an `InfluenceDomain` gate that admits the whole owning chain. Because the falloff is radial to the *clamped* segment, a point beyond a segment's start is measured as distance-to-endpoint, so the forearm's 3×-radius tube extends ~0.373 up the upper arm and blends up to 38% there.

## Proposed fix (chain-aware longitudinal gate) — needs a blend-width decision
Add a longitudinal gate: reject a segment candidate when the unclamped projection `tRaw = dot(v - start, ab)/|ab|²` falls outside `[-marginT, 1 + marginT]`, with `marginT = BlendMarginRadii * segment.Radius / segmentLength`. With `BlendMarginRadii = 1`, a bone blends roughly one radius past each of its own endpoints and not further, which is the "downstream only" behaviour requested.

Tradeoff to decide before implementing: this also tightens shoulder/hip/joint blending (a hard seam is possible if the margin is too small), and it changes the weight policy for every chain, so it needs body/limb/joint visual validation plus focused EditMode locality tests (upper-arm vertex beyond the band must get exactly zero forearm weight).

## Side observation
The scene still holds a stale `CreatureCreator Preview 2 (1)` rig with `IndexedBones.Count == 0` (an empty leftover after the duplicate cleanup). Worth a preview-ownership sweep (TSK-0104) — not part of this weighting change.

comments.body:
## Editor-configurable weighting policy + chain-aware gate implemented (2026-09-12)

User follow-up mandate: "Can we make this value configurable within the editor? I would like some other controls like these if possible or helpful". Implemented as a runtime policy plus live editor controls.

### New policy type (pure, Runtime)
`Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Animation/Binding/InfluenceWeightingPolicy.cs`:
- `RadiusScale` (default 3), `FalloffPower` (default 2), `FallbackBoneRadius` (default 0.5) — the TSK-0131 values, now tunable.
- `ChainAwareLocality` (default true) + `LongitudinalBlendMarginRadii` (default 1, bone radii) — the chain-aware gate.
- Constructor rejects non-finite / out-of-range values; `Default`, `Legacy`, `WithoutChainAwareLocality()`.

### Gate
`ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.FalloffFor` rejects a segment when the unclamped projection `tRaw` falls outside `[-marginT, 1+marginT]`, `marginT = marginRadii * radius / segmentLength`. A bone therefore reaches its own span plus a blend band past each endpoint, and nothing behind its own start. Verified on the live arm: an upper-arm vertex now gets **zero** forearm weight where it previously carried up to 0.383.
Totality: `Author` falls back to the ungated radial model for a vertex the gate would leave unweighted (and keeps the resolved-domain nearest-segment fallback after that), so no vertex is ever dropped. This fixed the new `CreatureSkinnedMeshRendererTests.Lifecycle_ValidRebind_ReplacesRendererWithoutLeaking` throw.

### Plumbing
- `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind(...)` gained an optional `InfluenceWeightingPolicy?`.
- `CreatureGenerationConfig` gained serialized **Skinning Weights** fields plus a clamped `WeightingPolicy`; verified the shared `Assets/Prefabs/CreatureGenerationConfig.asset` reads `3|2|0.5|true|1`.
- `CreatureRuntimePreview` and `CreaturePreviewController` (via a new `Func<InfluenceWeightingPolicy>` resolver) pass the config policy.
- `CreatureEditorWindow`: new **Skinning Weights** foldout in Editor Settings editing the shared asset and scheduling regeneration. Controls: Influence Radius Scale, Falloff Power, Default Bone Radius, Chain-Aware Locality, Blend Band (bone radii). Nothing touches DNA or the per-frame pose path.

### Validation
- EditMode **173/173** (9 new `InfluenceWeightingPolicyTests`, incl. the discriminating pair: default policy excludes the forearm at an upper-arm vertex, legacy includes it).
- PlayMode weight/skinning batch 35/40. The 5 failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this change:
  - `CreatureSkinnedMeshRendererTests` LBS-parity x2 + `body_j2` fixture (TSK-0194 clusters C/D).
  - `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoringTests.Author_MirroredTransition_...` — fixture passes `sourcePartId: "leg_mirror"` on a bone with `IsMirrored == true`, so `ResolveDomainId` yields `leg_mirror_mirror`, which the configured domain `leg_mirror` never admits. `MirrorSuffix == "_mirror"` confirms the mismatch; the domain filter is unchanged by this work.
  - `MorphologyInfluenceRadiusBridgeTests.BuildRadii_DegenerateFirstSegment_ClampsMidpointAtLowerBound` — expects 0.6, gets 0.4; `MorphologyInfluenceRadiusBridge` is untouched by this change.

### Residual
- Live shoulder/hip seam tuning is now the user's to make with the new controls; the gate tightens joints, so the Blend Band (or Chain-Aware Locality off) is the dial for shoulder softness.
- Editor UI interaction (sliders actually rebinding the preview) is a manual check; the data path is covered by unit tests and the asset read-back.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
## Live deformation report + mandate (2026-09-12) — joint-locality failures

### User Mandate (verbatim, STRICT)
> The knee is better than most, the elbow still moves the whole arm, the foot twists and compresses the whole leg, the tail moves in disjointed sections. The animation weights have been really buggy the whole time. I think we're doing it wrong. Capture these issues in the task system, along with the notes that we need to research the spore algorithms again

Capture verbatim; do not relax or re-scope.

### Observed symptom matrix (user, live editor)
| Joint posed | Observed | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Knee | "better than most" — closest to acceptable | local bend |
| Elbow | moves the whole arm | rotation confined to the elbow/forearm neighbourhood |
| Foot | twists and compresses the whole leg | local foot rotation; rest of the leg unaffected |
| Tail | moves in disjointed sections | continuous deformation along the tail |

### Assessment (leads, not diagnoses)
- All four are joint-localisation failures of the model this task already owns: closest-point-to-segment weighting with influence-domain eligibility, top-four influences, and `RadiusScale = 3` falloff.
- The knee being acceptable while the elbow leaks means the model is not uniformly wrong; the leaks are junction-specific. Candidates: domain eligibility across the limb chain, influence-radius overlap at tightly-packed joints, and the four-influence truncation dropping the correct segment. These are leads.
- "Disjointed sections" on the tail is consistent with hard nearest-wins at Body segment seams (documented simplification) as well as with compact Body segmentation count/placement. The segmentation half belongs to `TSK-0148` / `TSK-0171`; the seam-blend half belongs here.
- The user escalated to a design-level doubt: "the animation weights have been really buggy the whole time. I think we're doing it wrong." Treat as a model question, not a constant tweak.
- `TSK-0168`'s mandatory diagnosis protocol applies before any tuning: capture the top four influences per affected vertex, visualise the dominant influence, pose one bone at a time, and compare against the pure LBS oracle. Do not infer a weight bug from screenshots.

### Routing
- Deformation/locality mechanism (this report): **this task** (`TSK-0147`).
- Untouched-limb / cross-region deformation: `TSK-0168`.
- Body smear reproduction: `TSK-0172`.
- Body rig segmentation (tail disjoint): `TSK-0148`, `TSK-0171`.
- Skinning sweep diagnostics to evidence the above: `TSK-0169`.
- Spore algorithm re-research (research + recommendation, no constant changes): **`TSK-0222`**.

This comment extends the existing `dinus_uprightus` smear mandate already on this task; it does not supersede it.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Supersession risk flagged 2026-09-12 by the metaball pivot synthesis: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-spore-metaball-pivot-and-appearance-synthesis-2026-09-12.md` (report `CC-SYNTH-SPORE-PIVOT-20260912-A7E4D1`), findings F-01 and F-08.

This task owns the chain-aware-domain and tuning mechanism that the reported symptoms implicate. The synthesis concludes that tuning is the wrong lever: `ImplicitSurfaceInfluenceDomainResolver` selects the domain by nearest resolved part SDF and `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring` ranks by closest point on segment, and at a joint the geometric answer can be anatomically wrong.

Disposition: keep this task open. Do not archive it yet. Its diagnostics, gate behaviour, policy type, and editor controls remain useful and are reused by the new task TSK-0224 (provenance-attributed weights, child of TSK-0222). Whether the domain resolver is replaced or retained as a fallback inside an allowed chain is an open design question for TSK-0224.

Coordination request: TSK-0224 must not create a second policy type or a second domain resolver. Extend `InfluenceWeightingPolicy` with the joint-local transfer profile and reuse the existing gate structure.

Evidence supporting this disposition: the measured defect recorded on this task (323 upper-arm-dominant vertices, mean forearm weight 0.079, maximum 0.383, 61 vertices above 0.25) is exactly the symptom class that provenance attribution addresses structurally.

No code change made.
